headline.funnel_interpretation: Egger's test indicates no significant funnel plot asymmetry (p=0.8004). The distribution of studies appears symmetric, suggesting a lower risk of publication bias.
headline.results_interpretation: The pooled analysis of 11 studies yielded an effect size of 1.02 (95% CI: 0.98–1.07), indicating no statistically significant association between omega-3 fatty acids and prostate cancer. Although the point estimate suggests a potential positive relationship, the confidence interval includes the null. These findings were accompanied by substantial heterogeneity (I² = 72.89%), reflecting considerable variability across studies.
